$comment: Utility-AI weights (T-5.18, T-5.20). Score for an action = bias + sum(weight * consideration), every consideration normalised 0..1. Tuning lives here so it needs no recompile — see docs/DESIGN.md section 5 'The opponent AI'. A weight's SIGN is the interesting part: 'proximity: -0.5' on charge means charging is attractive when far away, not that being close is bad.

considerations.proximity: 1 at contact, 0 at maxRangeM or beyond
considerations.alignment: 1 nose exactly on the target, 0 facing directly away
considerations.ownHealth: 1 undamaged, 0 dead — mean part hp fraction
considerations.weaponSpin: 0..1 of the weapon's target rpm; 0 for a bot with no weapon
considerations.hazardNear: 1 on the lip of a pit, 0 at hazardRadiusM or beyond. hazardRadiusM was 2.4 until the T-4.9 balance pass, which is geometrically too late to be usable: the veto fired at 1.08 m from a pit CENTRE, but the nearest corner of the pit mouth is already 1.41 m out from that centre, so the bot was over the hole before it could react. 8 of 15 matchups ended in a pit. At 4.0 with pitVetoAt 0.35 the veto fires at 2.6 m, leaving about 1.2 m of margin outside the mouth - roughly the braking distance at cruising speed.
considerations.wallNear: 1 against a wall, 0 in the centre
considerations.foeHazard: 1 when the TARGET is on a pit lip — the push-it-in opportunity
considerations.stuck: 1 when we asked for throttle and barely moved
considerations.bladeDown: 1 - weaponSpin. Its own consideration because a NEGATIVE weight on weaponSpin contributes nothing when weaponSpin is already 0 — it can only penalise a spinning blade, never reward a stopped one. 'Spin up when the blade is slow' has to be said with a positive weight on the absence.
considerations.weaponLost: 1 when this bot has no usable weapon at all — none fitted, or its head has been sheared off. Distinct from bladeDown on purpose: a blade that is merely still spinning up wants spin-up, whereas a blade that is GONE wants ram, and one consideration covering both made every bot ram forever the moment a weapon was lost.
considerations.engaged: how long we have been nose-to-nose, over attackDwellSeconds. The signal that a grind is not working — the scripted AiDriver spent this as a hard ATTACK_DWELL timer; here it is a consideration, so breaking off competes with attacking instead of pre-empting it.

aggressive.$comment: Closes and stays closed. Ignores its own health almost entirely, so it will trade hits it should not. Beatable by out-ranging it.

defensive.$comment: Will not commit without a blade at speed, and disengages when hurt. Harder to burst down, but gives you room to set up.

opportunist.$comment: Circles at range and punishes a weakened or badly-placed opponent. The foeHealth weights are NEGATIVE on its attacks — a hurt target is what draws it in.

$difficultyNote: T-7.8. Difficulty is a MODIFIER over `tuning`, not a fourth personality. Personality is who the bot is; difficulty is how well it plays. Keeping them orthogonal means 'aggressive on easy' still reads as aggressive rather than as a different character, and it stops the weight tables tripling and drifting apart. NOTHING HERE CHEATS: no health, damage, mass or speed advantage is handed to the AI on hard, because a bot that wins by having more hp teaches the player nothing and feels unfair the moment they notice. Every lever below changes the QUALITY OF THE AI'S DECISIONS - how fast it reacts, how precisely it commits, how well it respects a pit, and how often it simply picks the wrong thing.

easy.$comment: Sluggish and imprecise, and it misjudges roughly a third of its decisions. It still plays its personality — it is just worse at it. hazardRadiusScale below 1 means it respects pits later, so it will occasionally drive itself in, which is the single most forgiving mistake an opponent can make.

normal.$comment: The tuning file exactly as authored and as balanced in T-4.9. All scales 1, no mistakes. This is the baseline every other difficulty is expressed against, so it must stay a pure pass-through.

hard.$comment: Re-decides almost twice as often, commits only on a tighter line, and gives pits a wider berth than a human reliably manages. No mistakes. It is not faster or stronger than you — it is more disciplined.
